title: Senior Staff Engineer Design
jobDescription:
Experience in Spec extraction, Architecture/Microarchitecture definition, Digital IP/Subsystem Design/Integration, Mixed signal IP Integration, So C Integration.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new ROLE:
  • Architecture Definition: Must be able to extract requirements from Specs, Partition requirements, define Architecture/microarchitecture.
  • Digital Lead: Must be able to act as a Digital functional lead for execution lead of IP/Sub-System or an So C.
  • Technical Expert: Must be able to provide Technical expertise on Digital Design, Architecture & Front-End flow.
  • Cross Functional Collaboration: Must be able to engage with various cross functional teams including Verification, Analog, Back-End, Marketing, Validation to ensure alignment on product objectives.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, such as Electronics, Digital Design, VLSI, So C Design.
  • Over 15 years of experience in Spec extraction, Architecture/Microarchitecture definition, Digital IP/Subsystem Design/Integration, Mixed signal IP Integration, So C Integration.
  • Strong technical knowledge of Front-End flows including Linting, CDC,RDC, Timing Constraints, Power intent, Synthesis, DFT, ATPG, Fault Grading, LEC, MVRC.
  • Good Understanding of Back-End flows including PNR, STA.
  • Strong Communication skills to interact with Cross functional teams and lead execution teams.
  • Good understanding of serial protocols like I2C, SPI, UART, PMBUS
  • Exposure to Point of Load converters, Gate driver controllers, PMICs etc.
  • Preferable understanding of Automotive Functional Safety standards.

Jyoti.Vimal@Infineon.com

title: Senior Staff Engineer Systems
jobDescription:
As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies.
  • Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage.
  • Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming.
  • Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C
  • Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential
  • Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc
  • Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage.
  • Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable.
  • Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus.
  • Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team.
  • Good communication and presentation skills.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence.
    • Your key responsibilities in would be
      a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence.
      b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment.
      c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams
      d. Hands on silicon bring-up
      e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem.
      f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT.
      g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow
      h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary
      i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies.
  • Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage.
  • Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming.
  • Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C
  • Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential
  • Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc
  • Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage.
  • Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable.
  • Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus.
  • Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team.
  • Good communication and presentation skills.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence.
    • Your key responsibilities in would be
      a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence.
      b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment.
      c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams
      d. Hands on silicon bring-up
      e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem.
      f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT.
      g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow
      h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary
      i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Type Hybrid Join as Professional As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies. Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage. Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming. Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage. Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable. Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus. Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team. Good communication and presentation skills. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence. Your key responsibilities in would be a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence. b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment. c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams d. Hands on silicon bring-up e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem. f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT. g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies. Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage. Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming. Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage. Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable. Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus. Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team. Good communication and presentation skills. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence. Your key responsibilities in would be a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence. b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment. c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams d. Hands on silicon bring-up e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues - working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis - while staying focused on the underlying problem. f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT. g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary. Contact: Anand Narendrakumar.Rawal@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener. Are you in? We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone. This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. At Infineon, we offer a working environment characterized by trust, openness, respect and tolerance and are committed to give all applicants and employees equal opportunities. We base our recruiting decisions on the applicant´s experience and skills. Learn more about our various contact channels. description:
As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies.
  • Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage.
  • Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming.
  • Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C
  • Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential
  • Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc
  • Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage.
  • Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable.
  • Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus.
  • Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team.
  • Good communication and presentation skills.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence.
    • Your key responsibilities in would be
      a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence.
      b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment.
      c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams
      d. Hands on silicon bring-up
      e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem.
      f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT.
      g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow
      h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary
      i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies.
  • Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage.
  • Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming.
  • Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C
  • Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential
  • Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc
  • Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage.
  • Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable.
  • Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus.
  • Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team.
  • Good communication and presentation skills.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence.
    • Your key responsibilities in would be
      a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence.
      b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment.
      c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams
      d. Hands on silicon bring-up
      e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem.
      f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT.
      g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow
      h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary
      i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Type Hybrid Join as Professional As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Development experience on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee technologies. Good understanding of BT, WLAN and Zig Bee protocols are added advantage. Sound basics in wireless communication systems and embedded system design / programming. Hands on experience of programming in Assembly language, C Good debugging skills in C, using gdb, analysing crashes using stack trace are essential Fair understanding of Wi FI debugging tools using Wireshark etc Understanding of Bluetooth sniffer logs are added advantage. Familiarity with IEEE 802.11 standards is desirable. Knowledge of Tcl/Python/System C would be plus. Ability to work with large, global, cross functional team. Good communication and presentation skills. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed As a member in WLAN MAC Coex systems team you will play a key role spanning from development, implementation and analyse results for BT-WLAN coexistence. Your key responsibilities in would be a. Design, analysis, development & maintenance of WLAN-BT-Zig Bee coexistence. b. Pre-Si design verification of Coex interfaces using scripting languages like TCL/python and validate in simulation environment. c. Working with various Cross functional teams like WL MAC, PHY systems, Firmware development, BT Stack, BT Firmware team and Hardware design teams d. Hands on silicon bring-up e. Debugging and solving cross layer customer issues – working across boundaries of WLAN MAC, BT sniffer analysis – while staying focused on the underlying problem. f. Understanding and modifying switch control logics between WLAN and BT. g. Identifying issues and proposing design and methodology improvements while driving compliance of existing design flow h. Mentoring and training other team members as necessary i. Creating collateral for internal and external use as necessary. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Principal Engineer Design
jobDescription:
#We Are In to transform theoretical concepts into real hardware designs. Are you in?

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Own No C IP microarchitecture, RTL generation, configuration and integration into So C
  • Deliver No C (Network on Chip)IP to internal consumers to enable prototyping, floor planning, synthesis, DFX verification
  • Perform quality checks with respective status assessment and reporting using tools like simulators, Lint, CDC
  • Work with methodology and tooling teams to identify and implement automation opportunities in the No C IP design workflow


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical or Electronics Engineering
  • 8+ years of experience in semiconductor product development, with strong technical expertise in digital design
  • Hands-on experience with No C IP microarchitecture, including RTL development, configuration, and So C-level integration
  • Expert-level knowledge of AMBA protocols such as AHB, AXI, and APB
  • Experience in low-power design methodologies is preferred
  • Proven track record of working across the complete IP development lifecycle
  • Familiarity with design quality tools such as CDC, Lint, and UPF
  • Strong debugging capabilities, ensuring No C designs are compile-clean, connectivity-clean, and meet quality standards
  • Advanced proficiency in System Verilog coding
  • Proactive and collaborative approach to risk identification and mitigation, with excellent communication and presentation skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, global environment with cross-functional teams including Architecture, IP, Physical Design, Verification, and DFX

title: Senior Specialist Data Engineer
jobDescription:
This is a key role within the DCI organization, in providing data integrity and insightful business analysis reports to support informed decision making in the space of customer journey growth. The ideal candidate comes with strong technical experience with business understanding and will work in the Analytics team delivering end-to-end storyboarding report solutions.

Your Role

  • Write, interpret, and optimize complex queries across disparate data sources using SQL to provide ad-hoc analysis to the stakeholders

title: Principal Engineer Digital Design
jobDescription:
The Multi Phase controller IP Lead is responsible for end-to-end definition, execution, and delivery of a control- and filter-centric signal processing digital IP that interfaces with high complexity AFEs. This role drives architecture closure across algorithm intent, fixed-point implementation, RTL micro-architecture, register/bus interfaces, verification strategy, and implementation readiness. The IP Lead aligns System modelling, Analog, RTL, DV, and DMS/AMS teams to ensure the IP meets functional, performance, latency, quality, and integration goals.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

Technical Ownership

  • Own end-to-end IP definition from requirements through architecture, implementation, verification, and handoff.
  • Translate system and product requirements into a clear IP micro-architecture and execution plan.
  • Drive closure on algorithm intent, control behavior, filter architecture, latency budgets, and implementation trade-offs.
  • Review and converge control/filter algorithm definition, sampling intent, and expected behavior with signal-processing architects.
  • Drive fixed-point architecture decisions including numeric precision, dynamic range, saturation, rounding, scaling, and pipeline placement.
  • Oversee RTL architecture for filter data path, coefficient programming, update paths, loop delays, state machines, and control logic.
  • Own top-level design decisions affecting timing, CDC, reset strategy, area, power, and implementation robustness.
  • Guide register architecture, status/control visibility, firmware programmability, and system integration behavior.
  • Drive architecture and RTL for AHB/PM Bus/AVS or other system-facing interfaces, including arbitration and error handling.
  • Define verification goals and signoff expectations jointly with DV and AMS verification leads.
  • Ensure availability of golden models, bit-true checking strategy, coverage goals, and end-to-end latency checks.
  • Drive closure on corner cases including overflow, convergence, saturation recovery, limit cycles, reset behavior, and protocol exceptions.
  • Ensure analog assumptions, abstraction boundaries, and mixed-signal interaction points are verified appropriately.
  • Review and close functional gaps across RTL, DV, DMS/AMS, and system validation.
  • Break down execution into work packages, milestones, dependencies, and risk mitigation plans.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering,
  • Strong experience leading digital or mixed-signal-adjacent IP development.
  • Strong understanding of control loops, DSP/filter implementations, or fixed-point digital signal processing.



Contact:
Vidhi Ashok.Thakkar@infineon.com

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} The Multi Phase controller IP Lead is responsible for end-to-end definition, execution, and delivery of a control- and filter-centric signal processing digital IP that interfaces with high complexity AFEs. This role drives architecture closure across algorithm intent, fixed-point implementation, RTL micro-architecture, register/bus interfaces, verification strategy, and implementation readiness. The IP Lead aligns System modelling, Analog, RTL, DV, and DMS/AMS teams to ensure the IP meets functional, performance, latency, quality, and integration goals.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

Technical Ownership

  • Own end-to-end IP definition from requirements through architecture, implementation, verification, and handoff.
  • Translate system and product requirements into a clear IP micro-architecture and execution plan.
  • Drive closure on algorithm intent, control behavior, filter architecture, latency budgets, and implementation trade-offs.
  • Review and converge control/filter algorithm definition, sampling intent, and expected behavior with signal-processing architects.
  • Drive fixed-point architecture decisions including numeric precision, dynamic range, saturation, rounding, scaling, and pipeline placement.
  • Oversee RTL architecture for filter data path, coefficient programming, update paths, loop delays, state machines, and control logic.
  • Own top-level design decisions affecting timing, CDC, reset strategy, area, power, and implementation robustness.
  • Guide register architecture, status/control visibility, firmware programmability, and system integration behavior.
  • Drive architecture and RTL for AHB/PM Bus/AVS or other system-facing interfaces, including arbitration and error handling.
  • Define verification goals and signoff expectations jointly with DV and AMS verification leads.
  • Ensure availability of golden models, bit-true checking strategy, coverage goals, and end-to-end latency checks.
  • Drive closure on corner cases including overflow, convergence, saturation recovery, limit cycles, reset behavior, and protocol exceptions.
  • Ensure analog assumptions, abstraction boundaries, and mixed-signal interaction points are verified appropriately.
  • Review and close functional gaps across RTL, DV, DMS/AMS, and system validation.
  • Break down execution into work packages, milestones, dependencies, and risk mitigation plans.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering,
  • Strong experience leading digital or mixed-signal-adjacent IP development.
  • Strong understanding of control loops, DSP/filter implementations, or fixed-point digital signal processing.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

If you believe you belong to any of the categories of protected Veterans listed above, please indicate by checking the appropriate box below. The Multi Phase controller IP Lead is responsible for end-to-end definition, execution, and delivery of a control- and filter-centric signal processing digital IP that interfaces with high complexity AFEs. This role drives architecture closure across algorithm intent, fixed-point implementation, RTL micro-architecture, register/bus interfaces, verification strategy, and implementation readiness. The IP Lead aligns System modelling, Analog, RTL, DV, and DMS/AMS teams to ensure the IP meets functional, performance, latency, quality, and integration goals. Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Technical Ownership Own end-to-end IP definition from requirements through architecture, implementation, verification, and handoff. Translate system and product requirements into a clear IP micro-architecture and execution plan. Drive closure on algorithm intent, control behavior, filter architecture, latency budgets, and implementation trade-offs. Review and converge control/filter algorithm definition, sampling intent, and expected behavior with signal-processing architects. Drive fixed-point architecture decisions including numeric precision, dynamic range, saturation, rounding, scaling, and pipeline placement. Oversee RTL architecture for filter data path, coefficient programming, update paths, loop delays, state machines, and control logic. Own top-level design decisions affecting timing, CDC, reset strategy, area, power, and implementation robustness. Guide register architecture, status/control visibility, firmware programmability, and system integration behavior. Drive architecture and RTL for AHB/PM Bus/AVS or other system-facing interfaces, including arbitration and error handling. Define verification goals and signoff expectations jointly with DV and AMS verification leads. Ensure availability of golden models, bit-true checking strategy, coverage goals, and end-to-end latency checks. Drive closure on corner cases including overflow, convergence, saturation recovery, limit cycles, reset behavior, and protocol exceptions. Ensure analog assumptions, abstraction boundaries, and mixed-signal interaction points are verified appropriately. Review and close functional gaps across RTL, DV, DMS/AMS, and system validation. Break down execution into work packages, milestones, dependencies, and risk mitigation plans. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Strong experience leading digital or mixed-signal-adjacent IP development. Strong understanding of control loops, DSP/filter implementations, or fixed-point digital signal processing. Contact: Vidhi Ashok.Thakkar@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener. Are you in? We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone. This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. description:
The Multi Phase controller IP Lead is responsible for end-to-end definition, execution, and delivery of a control- and filter-centric signal processing digital IP that interfaces with high complexity AFEs. This role drives architecture closure across algorithm intent, fixed-point implementation, RTL micro-architecture, register/bus interfaces, verification strategy, and implementation readiness. The IP Lead aligns System modelling, Analog, RTL, DV, and DMS/AMS teams to ensure the IP meets functional, performance, latency, quality, and integration goals.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

Technical Ownership

  • Own end-to-end IP definition from requirements through architecture, implementation, verification, and handoff.
  • Translate system and product requirements into a clear IP micro-architecture and execution plan.
  • Drive closure on algorithm intent, control behavior, filter architecture, latency budgets, and implementation trade-offs.
  • Review and converge control/filter algorithm definition, sampling intent, and expected behavior with signal-processing architects.
  • Drive fixed-point architecture decisions including numeric precision, dynamic range, saturation, rounding, scaling, and pipeline placement.
  • Oversee RTL architecture for filter data path, coefficient programming, update paths, loop delays, state machines, and control logic.
  • Own top-level design decisions affecting timing, CDC, reset strategy, area, power, and implementation robustness.
  • Guide register architecture, status/control visibility, firmware programmability, and system integration behavior.
  • Drive architecture and RTL for AHB/PM Bus/AVS or other system-facing interfaces, including arbitration and error handling.
  • Define verification goals and signoff expectations jointly with DV and AMS verification leads.
  • Ensure availability of golden models, bit-true checking strategy, coverage goals, and end-to-end latency checks.
  • Drive closure on corner cases including overflow, convergence, saturation recovery, limit cycles, reset behavior, and protocol exceptions.
  • Ensure analog assumptions, abstraction boundaries, and mixed-signal interaction points are verified appropriately.
  • Review and close functional gaps across RTL, DV, DMS/AMS, and system validation.
  • Break down execution into work packages, milestones, dependencies, and risk mitigation plans.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering,
  • Strong experience leading digital or mixed-signal-adjacent IP development.
  • Strong understanding of control loops, DSP/filter implementations, or fixed-point digital signal processing.



Contact:
Vidhi Ashok.Thakkar@infineon.com

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} The Multi Phase controller IP Lead is responsible for end-to-end definition, execution, and delivery of a control- and filter-centric signal processing digital IP that interfaces with high complexity AFEs. This role drives architecture closure across algorithm intent, fixed-point implementation, RTL micro-architecture, register/bus interfaces, verification strategy, and implementation readiness. The IP Lead aligns System modelling, Analog, RTL, DV, and DMS/AMS teams to ensure the IP meets functional, performance, latency, quality, and integration goals.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

Technical Ownership

  • Own end-to-end IP definition from requirements through architecture, implementation, verification, and handoff.
  • Translate system and product requirements into a clear IP micro-architecture and execution plan.
  • Drive closure on algorithm intent, control behavior, filter architecture, latency budgets, and implementation trade-offs.
  • Review and converge control/filter algorithm definition, sampling intent, and expected behavior with signal-processing architects.
  • Drive fixed-point architecture decisions including numeric precision, dynamic range, saturation, rounding, scaling, and pipeline placement.
  • Oversee RTL architecture for filter data path, coefficient programming, update paths, loop delays, state machines, and control logic.
  • Own top-level design decisions affecting timing, CDC, reset strategy, area, power, and implementation robustness.
  • Guide register architecture, status/control visibility, firmware programmability, and system integration behavior.
  • Drive architecture and RTL for AHB/PM Bus/AVS or other system-facing interfaces, including arbitration and error handling.
  • Define verification goals and signoff expectations jointly with DV and AMS verification leads.
  • Ensure availability of golden models, bit-true checking strategy, coverage goals, and end-to-end latency checks.
  • Drive closure on corner cases including overflow, convergence, saturation recovery, limit cycles, reset behavior, and protocol exceptions.
  • Ensure analog assumptions, abstraction boundaries, and mixed-signal interaction points are verified appropriately.
  • Review and close functional gaps across RTL, DV, DMS/AMS, and system validation.
  • Break down execution into work packages, milestones, dependencies, and risk mitigation plans.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering,
  • Strong experience leading digital or mixed-signal-adjacent IP development.
  • Strong understanding of control loops, DSP/filter implementations, or fixed-point digital signal processing.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Senior Staff Engineer Verification
jobDescription:
Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Verification of complex So Cs / IPs and provide technical leadership to the team while creating test plans and test bench architecture.
  • Development of constraint-random verification environment at both sub-system and So C level.
  • Develop expertise in multiple areas of verification – RTL, Gate level and Power aware simulations
  • Drive verification closure on complex modules and So Cs using SV/UVM based methodology.
  • Schedule management and handling cross functional team interactions
  • Should be a good mentor and guide for junior engineers in the team


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Electrical/Electronic Engineering Bachelor's - 9 to 11 years’ experience, Master’s - 8 to 10 years’ experience
  • In depth understanding of ASIC verification concepts and techniques. Ability to architect complex module / sub system / full chip test benches and build verification infrastructure in SV/UVM.
  • Should be a good mentor and guide the junior engineers in the team.
  • Experience in ARM based So C verification covering RTL, Power Aware and Gate level simulations is a plus.
  • Good knowledge in industry standard protocols is preferable

title: Staff Engineer Verification
jobDescription:
Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create Subsystem Verification plan for PMBUS, AVS interface and signoff protocol compliance
  • Formal verification coverage of critical control interfaces
  • SV, UVM based Verification environment.
  • RNM based simulation, Matlab model’s integration - DPI in Verification strategy.
  • SOC Integration verification and system level scenarios development
  • GLS Verification including root causing down to flop level
  • Code Coverage, functional coverage
  • Fault Injection Campaign Execution for ASIL-D Products
  • Familiarity with industry standard protocols like I2C/I3C, UART, AHB/APB, SMBUS, SPI.

title: Software Engineer for Documentation with Automotive Microcontroller (MC) (f/m/div)*
jobDescription:
Join our Documentation Enablement & Infrastructure team as a key contributor. You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving ‘can do’ attitu

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver
  • Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation
  • Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required
  • Support and mentor team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • A degree in a related field such as computer science
  • Strong SW programming skills
    • Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...)
    • Good understanding of XML
    • Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge
    • Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies
    • MCP implementation experience
    • Git / Gitlab expert knowledge
    • Jenkins knowledge
  • Pro-active but process focussed
  • Confident presentation skills
  • A team player
  • Adaptable as business demands change
  • Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation
  • Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential)
    • A willingness to continuously learn

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving ‘can do’ attitu

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver
  • Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation
  • Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required
  • Support and mentor team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • A degree in a related field such as computer science
  • Strong SW programming skills
    • Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...)
    • Good understanding of XML
    • Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge
    • Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies
    • MCP implementation experience
    • Git / Gitlab expert knowledge
    • Jenkins knowledge
  • Pro-active but process focussed
  • Confident presentation skills
  • A team player
  • Adaptable as business demands change
  • Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation
  • Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential)
    • A willingness to continuously learn

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving ‘can do’ attitu Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required Support and mentor team members Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed A degree in a related field such as computer science Strong SW programming skills Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...) Good understanding of XML Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies MCP implementation experience Git / Gitlab expert knowledge Jenkins knowledge Pro-active but process focussed Confident presentation skills A team player Adaptable as business demands change Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential) A willingness to continuously learn Contact: Pooja.Ananda Chowta@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

originalTitle: Software Engineer for Documentation with Automotive Microcontroller (MC) (f/m/div)*

experienceProfile.rawText:
Join our Documentation Enablement & Infrastructure team as a key contributor. You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving 'can do' attitu Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required Support and mentor team members Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed A degree in a related field such as computer science Strong SW programming skills Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...) Good understanding of XML Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies MCP implementation experience Git / Gitlab expert knowledge Jenkins knowledge Pro-active but process focussed Confident presentation skills A team player Adaptable as business demands change Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential) A willingness to continuously learn Contact: Pooja.Ananda Chowta@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener. Are you in? We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone. This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. At Infineon, we offer a working environment characterized by trust, openness, respect and tolerance and are committed to give all applicants and employees equal opportunities. We base our recruiting decisions on the applicant´s experience and skills. Learn more about our various contact channels. Please let your recruiter know if they need to pay special attention to something in order to enable your participation in the interview process. Click here for more information about Diversity & Inclusion at Infineon.
