description:
Join our Documentation Enablement & Infrastructure team as a key contributor. You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving ‘can do’ attitu

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver
  • Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation
  • Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required
  • Support and mentor team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • A degree in a related field such as computer science
  • Strong SW programming skills
    • Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...)
    • Good understanding of XML
    • Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge
    • Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies
    • MCP implementation experience
    • Git / Gitlab expert knowledge
    • Jenkins knowledge
  • Pro-active but process focussed
  • Confident presentation skills
  • A team player
  • Adaptable as business demands change
  • Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation
  • Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential)
    • A willingness to continuously learn

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} Join our Documentation Enablement & Infrastructure team as a key contributor. You'll document complex, leading-edge automotive products using state-of-the-art tools and practices while collaborating with engineering teams worldwide. We focus on digitalization and automation, proactively developing agile documentation solutions that meet current and long-term company needs. You will have an eye for detail, be a team player, but demonstrate initiative, be flexible as situations and deadlines demand, be responsible, organized, follow the company and business unit standards, and bring a problem solving ‘can do’ attitu

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Provide SW solutions to support all aspects of the technical documentation flow, extracting information from source databases, manipulating content to required standards, building reports, and preparing content to interact with AI solutions that you deliver
  • Learn the documentation lifecycle from information creation to external release at given milestones, to help identify and support custom solutions, understanding the different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Ensure the quality and consistency of our SW solutions which in turn guarantee the reliability of our documentation
  • Roll-out solutions to documentation, engineering, and technical marketing teams, as required
  • Support and mentor team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • A degree in a related field such as computer science
  • Strong SW programming skills
    • Python (Num Py, pandas, XML libraries, ...)
    • Good understanding of XML
    • Practical and demonstratable AI/ML knowledge
    • Understanding of Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies
    • MCP implementation experience
    • Git / Gitlab expert knowledge
    • Jenkins knowledge
  • Pro-active but process focussed
  • Confident presentation skills
  • A team player
  • Adaptable as business demands change
  • Basic understanding of a Component Content Management System (CCMS) and the concept of modular documentation
  • Fluency in English with good written and verbal communication skills (German is helpful, but not essential)
    • A willingness to continuously learn

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

If you believe you belong to any of the categories of protected Veterans listed above, please indicate by checking the appropriate box below. title: Documentation Engineer
jobDescription:
#We Are In to strive to offer the #1 digital customer experience at Infineon. Are you in? Join our Documentation Enablement & Infrastructure (DEI) team and you will be helping document complex, leading edge, automotive microcontroller products using state of the art documentation tools and practices, interacting with engineering teams world-wide. Our focus is digitalization and automation, pro-actively developing agile documentation solutions that meet the needs now and in the future.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Be responsible for documentation deliverables that meet the required documentation standards and processes
  • Contribute to the documentation content architecture to handle different product families, multiple product variants, and numerous document types
  • Pro-actively drive the workflow from information creation to external release at given milestones, working closely with SMEs
  • Convert and standardize documentation to the meet the company and business unit policies and best practice
  • Create graphics to the required standards
  • Ensure the quality and consistency of our documentation
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Mentor junior members of the team
  • Support and train engineers as necessary to work with the company CCMS and contribute to the documentation flows
    • Actively participate in knowledge sharing and development of best practices with other team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • A degree in a related field such as computer science, technical communication, or electrical engineering
  • Excellent written and spoken English language skills
  • Minimum 5+ years of relavent experience
  • Strong technical skills with the ability to learn quickly
  • A methodical approach and keen eye for detail
  • Recent and practical knowledge of DITA XML
  • A demonstrable understanding and knowledge of the concept of modular documentation
  • Recent and practical experience of a Component Content Management System (CCMS)
  • Recent experience and knowledge of a version control systems such as Git
  • Ability to work with cross-functional teams across multiple sites
  • Flexibility to quickly respond to higher priority concerns
  • A willingness to continuously learn
  • Good to have:
    • XSLT knowledge (writing and running)
    • Writing regular expressions
    • Familiarity with JIRA
    • Coding skills, particularly python
    • Knowledge of Jenkins
    • Gitlab knowledge
    • AI/LLM experience and understanding

Gowri Shenoy, Linked In

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} We are hiring for Technical writer with strong hands on exposure in Component Content Management System (CCMS). Should be good with version control systems such as Git. Must have excellent written and spoken English language skills and knowing German will be added advantage.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Responsible for documentation deliverables that meet the required documentation standards and processes
  • Pro-actively drive the workflow from information creation to external release at given milestones, working closely with SMES
  • Convert and standardize documentation to the meet the company and business unit policies and best practice
  • Create graphics to the required standards and ensure the quality and consistency of our documentation
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Support and train engineers as necessary to work with the company CCMS and contribute to the documentation flows
  • Actively participate in knowledge sharing and development of best practices with other team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • Must have degree in a related field such as computer science, technical communication, or electrical engineering
  • Should have strong hold on English language verbal & written both. Expertise in German language will be added advantage.
  • Strong technical skills with the ability to learn quickly with methodical approach and keen eye for details
  • Hands on experience and practical knowledge of DITA XML is must.
  • A demonstrable understanding and knowledge of the concept of modular documentation
  • Practical experience of a Component Content Management System(CCMS)is must.
  • Must have strong exposure of a version control systems such as Git
  • Ability to work with cross-functional teams across multiple sites
  • Flexibility to quickly respond to higher priority concerns and willingness to continuously learn
  • Exposure in XSLT,JIRA, good programming skills particularly python and knowledge of Jenkins will be added advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

We are hiring for Technical writer with strong hands on exposure in Component Content Management System (CCMS). Should be good with version control systems such as Git. Must have excellent written and spoken English language skills and knowing German will be added advantage. Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Responsible for documentation deliverables that meet the required documentation standards and processes Pro-actively drive the workflow from information creation to external release at given milestones, working closely with SMES Convert and standardize documentation to the meet the company and business unit policies and best practice Create graphics to the required standards and ensure the quality and consistency of our documentation Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries Support and train engineers as necessary to work with the company CCMS and contribute to the documentation flows Actively participate in knowledge sharing and development of best practices with other team members Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Must have degree in a related field such as computer science, technical communication, or electrical engineering Should have strong hold on English language verbal & written both. Expertise in German language will be added advantage. Strong technical skills with the ability to learn quickly with methodical approach and keen eye for details Hands on experience and practical knowledge of DITA XML is must. A demonstrable understanding and knowledge of the concept of modular documentation Practical experience of a Component Content Management System(CCMS)is must. Must have strong exposure of a version control systems such as Git Ability to work with cross-functional teams across multiple sites Flexibility to quickly respond to higher priority concerns and willingness to continuously learn Exposure in XSLT,JIRA, good programming skills particularly python and knowledge of Jenkins will be added advantage. description:
We are hiring for Technical writer with strong hands on exposure in Component Content Management System (CCMS). Should be good with version control systems such as Git. Must have excellent written and spoken English language skills and knowing German will be added advantage.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Responsible for documentation deliverables that meet the required documentation standards and processes
  • Pro-actively drive the workflow from information creation to external release at given milestones, working closely with SMES
  • Convert and standardize documentation to the meet the company and business unit policies and best practice
  • Create graphics to the required standards and ensure the quality and consistency of our documentation
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Support and train engineers as necessary to work with the company CCMS and contribute to the documentation flows
  • Actively participate in knowledge sharing and development of best practices with other team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • Must have degree in a related field such as computer science, technical communication, or electrical engineering
  • Should have strong hold on English language verbal & written both. Expertise in German language will be added advantage.
  • Strong technical skills with the ability to learn quickly with methodical approach and keen eye for details
  • Hands on experience and practical knowledge of DITA XML is must.
  • A demonstrable understanding and knowledge of the concept of modular documentation
  • Practical experience of a Component Content Management System(CCMS)is must.
  • Must have strong exposure of a version control systems such as Git
  • Ability to work with cross-functional teams across multiple sites
  • Flexibility to quickly respond to higher priority concerns and willingness to continuously learn
  • Exposure in XSLT,JIRA, good programming skills particularly python and knowledge of Jenkins will be added advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} We are hiring for Technical writer with strong hands on exposure in Component Content Management System (CCMS). Should be good with version control systems such as Git. Must have excellent written and spoken English language skills and knowing German will be added advantage.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role
  • Responsible for documentation deliverables that meet the required documentation standards and processes
  • Pro-actively drive the workflow from information creation to external release at given milestones, working closely with SMES
  • Convert and standardize documentation to the meet the company and business unit policies and best practice
  • Create graphics to the required standards and ensure the quality and consistency of our documentation
  • Contribute solutions and ideas to improving the efficiency and accuracy of our documentation deliveries
  • Support and train engineers as necessary to work with the company CCMS and contribute to the documentation flows
  • Actively participate in knowledge sharing and development of best practices with other team members


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
  • Must have degree in a related field such as computer science, technical communication, or electrical engineering
  • Should have strong hold on English language verbal & written both. Expertise in German language will be added advantage.
  • Strong technical skills with the ability to learn quickly with methodical approach and keen eye for details
  • Hands on experience and practical knowledge of DITA XML is must.
  • A demonstrable understanding and knowledge of the concept of modular documentation
  • Practical experience of a Component Content Management System(CCMS)is must.
  • Must have strong exposure of a version control systems such as Git
  • Ability to work with cross-functional teams across multiple sites
  • Flexibility to quickly respond to higher priority concerns and willingness to continuously learn
  • Exposure in XSLT,JIRA, good programming skills particularly python and knowledge of Jenkins will be added advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Senior Specialist Project Management Office
jobDescription:
#We Are In​ for managing, leading, and being experts – all at once.​ Are you in?

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Collect, document, and validate business requirements for PMO initiatives and projects
  • Translate business needs into functional specifications and process documentation
  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of PMO standards, methodologies and processes
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and reports to monitor KPIs, project health, and portfolio performance
  • Conduct variance analysis, trend analysis, and forecasting to support decision-making
  • Provide analytical support for portfolio prioritization, risk management, and resource planning


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Informatics or a related discipline
  • 3–5 years of experience in business analysis and/or data analytics, preferably within a PMO or project-driven environment
  • Strong experience in data analysis tools (e.g., Microsoft Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau)
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
  • Ability to lead initiatives, manage stakeholders and work effectively in a highly collaborative Project Management Office environment
  • Exceptional communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts to diverse audiences


#We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization.
As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener.
Are you in?

We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone.
This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. At Infineon, we offer a working environment characterized by trust, openness, respect and tolerance and are committed to give all applicants and employees equal opportunities. We base our recruiting decisions on the applicant´s experience and skills. Learn more about our various contact channels.
Please let your recruiter know if they need to pay special attention to something in order to enable your participation in the interview process.
Click here for more information about Diversity & Inclusion at Infineon.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Collect, document, and validate business requirements for PMO initiatives and projects
  • Translate business needs into functional specifications and process documentation
  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of PMO standards, methodologies and processes
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and reports to monitor KPIs, project health, and portfolio performance
  • Conduct variance analysis, trend analysis, and forecasting to support decision-making
  • Provide analytical support for portfolio prioritization, risk management, and resource planning


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Informatics or a related discipline
  • 3–5 years of experience in business analysis and/or data analytics, preferably within a PMO or project-driven environment
  • Strong experience in data analysis tools (e.g., Microsoft Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau)
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
  • Ability to lead initiatives, manage stakeholders and work effectively in a highly collaborative Project Management Office environment
  • Exceptional communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts to diverse audiences

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

#We Are In​ for managing, leading, and being experts – all at once.​ Are you in?

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Collect, document, and validate business requirements for PMO initiatives and projects
  • Translate business needs into functional specifications and process documentation
  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of PMO standards, methodologies and processes
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and reports to monitor KPIs, project health, and portfolio performance
  • Conduct variance analysis, trend analysis, and forecasting to support decision-making
  • Provide analytical support for portfolio prioritization, risk management, and resource planning


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Informatics or a related discipline
  • 3–5 years of experience in business analysis and/or data analytics, preferably within a PMO or project-driven environment
  • Strong experience in data analysis tools (e.g., Microsoft Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau)
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
  • Ability to lead initiatives, manage stakeholders and work effectively in a highly collaborative Project Management Office environment
  • Exceptional communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts to diverse audiences


#We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization.
As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener.
Are you in?

We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone.
This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. At Infineon, we offer a working environment characterized by trust, openness, respect and tolerance and are committed to give all applicants and employees equal opportunities. We base our recruiting decisions on the applicant´s experience and skills. Learn more about our various contact channels.
Please let your recruiter know if they need to pay special attention to something in order to enable your participation in the interview process.
Click here for more information about Diversity & Inclusion at Infineon.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Product Owner Hardware Web Experience

experienceProfile.rawText:
We are seeking an experienced and skilled Product Owner Hardware Web Experience to join our agile team. As a Product Owner Hardware Web Experience, you will be responsible for managing the Boards and Kits experience on the infineon.com website with significant complexity, risk, and impact. Your primary focus will be on proactively optimizing the developer web experience of these pages to maximize business value and reach departmental goals. You will be gathering and prioritizing stakeholder requirements, interacting with web users to understand customer needs, and leading the development of new web functionalities Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Own the complete end-to-end customer journey on infineon.com (covering web functionalities for products such as evaluation boards, the Evaluation Board Finder tool, and related digital experiences) Understand developer needs through data analysis, CX reports and other tools and develop solutions to meet those needs Identify changes in user behavior and adapt the web product approach as needed Continuously collect and review new requirements from stakeholders (e.g., divisions, marketing, sales, and product teams) Coordinate with management to adjust web plans and roadmap as needed Lead the development of new web functionalities, including ideation, prototyping, and customer validation, with a focus on user experience and quality assurance Manage, refine, and prioritize the web features product backlog continuously Accountable for product release, and ensuring product success Analyze and evaluate web data to identify optimization opportunities and develop A/B testing plans Coordinate stakeholder communication on business goals, market opportunities, and priorities in the web area. Collaborate closely with other web owners and central departments (e.g. UX/UI, CX, Analytics, IT) Continuously improve process quality and evaluate web progress and user satisfaction Monitor new trends and technologies Continuously monitor changes in the Infineon competitive environment Serve as a resource for less experienced Product Owners Web Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Proven track record as a Product Owner in agile environments, ideally for customer-facing web platforms, portals, or digital tools in high-tech/B2B contexts. Proven track record in Printed Circuit Board (PCB) development with Altium, Cadence, Ki Cad or similar layout software and simulation tools (PSpice, LTspice, SIMetrix, etc.) Significant experience in at least one of the following areas (strongly preferred): Prior engineering role at a semiconductor company, with a proven track record of supporting customers to achieve design wins (securing adoption of company products into customer designs and driving them through to production) Hands-on development of production-level hardware systems, including board-level design, system integration, validation, and successful transition to volume manufacturing. Bonus multiplier: Proven involvement with AI-based acceleration technologies for hardware design-such as AI-augmented EDA flows, agentic AI for chip optimization, accelerated power/performance analysis, generative AI in design workflows, or AI-powered digital twins/portals that compress design cycles and enable faster hardware innovation. MBA from a reputable business school (top-tier preferred). Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills Candidates who have worked in the semiconductor market would be a plus Ability to analyze data and make informed decisions Strong problem-solving and prioritization skills Experience with A/B testing and experimentation Knowledge of web analytics tools and methodologies Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities Strong collaboration and teamwork skills Contact: Pooja.Ananda Chowta@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener. Are you in? We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone. This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. title: Staff Personalization Specialist - SF and Adobe Target
jobDescription:
The role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences.
  • Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses.
  • Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability.
  • Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences.
  • Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog.
  • Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms.
  • Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others.
  • Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly.
  • Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} The role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences.
  • Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses.
  • Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability.
  • Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences.
  • Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog.
  • Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms.
  • Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others.
  • Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly.
  • Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience. Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences. Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses. Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability. Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences. Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements. Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog. Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation. Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field. Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms. Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others. Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly. Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

normalizedTitle: Staff Personalization Specialist - SF and Adobe Target
jobCategory: Staff Personalization Specialist - SF and Adobe Target
description:
The role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences.
  • Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses.
  • Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability.
  • Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences.
  • Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog.
  • Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms.
  • Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others.
  • Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly.
  • Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.
