Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} The role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences.
  • Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses.
  • Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability.
  • Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences.
  • Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog.
  • Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms.
  • Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others.
  • Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly.
  • Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

role involves designing, executing, and analyzing personalization and A/B testing use cases across multiple channels to deliver targeted customer experiences, while collaborating with various stakeholders to identify opportunities and optimize results. The ideal candidate will leverage technical expertise, data analysis, and industry knowledge to drive personalization strategies, troubleshoot issues, generate insights through data analysis, and continuously improve the overall customer experience. Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Design and execute personalization and A/B Testing use cases across multiple channels such as website, email, search, social media, and others, including audience creation, creating targeted content, and activation of personalized customer experiences. Test and analyze A/B testing and experimentation plans to validate personalization hypotheses. Manage and maintain recommendation services (e.g. recommendation engines, dynamic content delivery) and personalized UI components, ensuring seamless integration and scalability. Collaborate with data engineers to ingest, transform, and activate user data for personalized experiences. Analyze and optimize testing and personalization use cases to measure the effectiveness, troubleshooting issues and providing recommendations for future improvements. Partner with business stakeholders to identify new opportunities for personalization, translate them into actionable concepts and strategy plans, and prioritize use cases and manage the backlog. Collaborate with IT teams to implement and troubleshoot personalization activities, including incident management and technical implementation. Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best-practices for personalization and marketing automation, and apply this knowledge to continuously improve our personalization strategies. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field. Minimum 5+ years of work experience in executing personalization activities across channels, including experience with personalization tools, marketing automation platforms, and customer data platforms. Proficiency in using personalization tools such as Adobe Target, Salesforce Personalization, or others. Strong understanding of marketing principles including customer segmentation, targeting, and data analysis. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Powerpoint, and ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly. Passion for creating meaningful, user-centric experiences. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Product Quality Manager
jobDescription:
Product Quality Manager with experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create qualification plans, developing them according to the relevant standards (e.g. AEC-Q100) in cooperation with the stakeholders and also taking customer aspects into account, always ensuring that agreed deadlines and costs are met.
  • Be responsible for quality reporting to our internal customers.
  • Be the responsible quality manager and contact person for quality issues, when it comes to volume production.
  • Work very closely with both the business unit and our production sites distributed around the world.
  • Check compliance with defined quality standards and quality assurance guidelines, operating an active risk management.
  • Support cross-departmental teams to solve possible escalation cases, if needed.
  • Derive future quality targets from customer requirements and market trends.
  • Continuously improve quality-related activities and methods.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry;
  • Good experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Quality background would be appreciated.
  • Good understanding of the structure and function of microcontroller products.
  • Good understanding of quality methods (e.g. FMEA, 8D, 3x5why, APQP);
  • Intercultural competence, as working with international, global teams and customers is an integral part of the job.
  • Availability to travel occasionally.
  • Fluency in English.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create qualification plans, developing them according to the relevant standards (e.g. AEC-Q100) in cooperation with the stakeholders and also taking customer aspects into account, always ensuring that agreed deadlines and costs are met.
  • Be responsible for quality reporting to our internal customers.
  • Be the responsible quality manager and contact person for quality issues, when it comes to volume production.
  • Work very closely with both the business unit and our production sites distributed around the world.
  • Check compliance with defined quality standards and quality assurance guidelines, operating an active risk management.
  • Support cross-departmental teams to solve possible escalation cases, if needed.
  • Derive future quality targets from customer requirements and market trends.
  • Continuously improve quality-related activities and methods.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry;
  • Good experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Quality background would be appreciated.
  • Good understanding of the structure and function of microcontroller products.
  • Good understanding of quality methods (e.g. FMEA, 8D, 3x5why, APQP);
  • Intercultural competence, as working with international, global teams and customers is an integral part of the job.
  • Availability to travel occasionally.
  • Fluency in English.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Product Quality Manager with experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Create qualification plans, developing them according to the relevant standards (e.g. AEC-Q100) in cooperation with the stakeholders and also taking customer aspects into account, always ensuring that agreed deadlines and costs are met. Be responsible for quality reporting to our internal customers. Be the responsible quality manager and contact person for quality issues, when it comes to volume production. Work very closely with both the business unit and our production sites distributed around the world. Check compliance with defined quality standards and quality assurance guidelines, operating an active risk management. Support cross-departmental teams to solve possible escalation cases, if needed. Derive future quality targets from customer requirements and market trends. Continuously improve quality-related activities and methods. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry; Good experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Quality background would be appreciated. Good understanding of the structure and function of microcontroller products. Good understanding of quality methods (e.g. FMEA, 8D, 3x5why, APQP); Intercultural competence, as working with international, global teams and customers is an integral part of the job. Availability to travel occasionally. Fluency in English. Contact: Pooja.Ananda Chowta@infineon.com #We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization. As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener. Are you in? We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone. This means we embrace diversity and inclusion and welcome everyone for who they are. At Infineon, we offer a working environment characterized by trust, openness, respect and tolerance and are committed to give all applicants and employees equal opportunities. We base our recruiting decisions on the applicant´s experience and skills. Learn more about our various contact channels. description:
Product Quality Manager with experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create qualification plans, developing them according to the relevant standards (e.g. AEC-Q100) in cooperation with the stakeholders and also taking customer aspects into account, always ensuring that agreed deadlines and costs are met.
  • Be responsible for quality reporting to our internal customers.
  • Be the responsible quality manager and contact person for quality issues, when it comes to volume production.
  • Work very closely with both the business unit and our production sites distributed around the world.
  • Check compliance with defined quality standards and quality assurance guidelines, operating an active risk management.
  • Support cross-departmental teams to solve possible escalation cases, if needed.
  • Derive future quality targets from customer requirements and market trends.
  • Continuously improve quality-related activities and methods.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry;
  • Good experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Quality background would be appreciated.
  • Good understanding of the structure and function of microcontroller products.
  • Good understanding of quality methods (e.g. FMEA, 8D, 3x5why, APQP);
  • Intercultural competence, as working with international, global teams and customers is an integral part of the job.
  • Availability to travel occasionally.
  • Fluency in English.

Pooja.Ananda Chowta@infineon.com

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create qualification plans, developing them according to the relevant standards (e.g. AEC-Q100) in cooperation with the stakeholders and also taking customer aspects into account, always ensuring that agreed deadlines and costs are met.
  • Be responsible for quality reporting to our internal customers.
  • Be the responsible quality manager and contact person for quality issues, when it comes to volume production.
  • Work very closely with both the business unit and our production sites distributed around the world.
  • Check compliance with defined quality standards and quality assurance guidelines, operating an active risk management.
  • Support cross-departmental teams to solve possible escalation cases, if needed.
  • Derive future quality targets from customer requirements and market trends.
  • Continuously improve quality-related activities and methods.


Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry;
  • Good experience in the field of semiconductors, Microcontroller within the automotive industry. Quality background would be appreciated.
  • Good understanding of the structure and function of microcontroller products.
  • Good understanding of quality methods (e.g. FMEA, 8D, 3x5why, APQP);
  • Intercultural competence, as working with international, global teams and customers is an integral part of the job.
  • Availability to travel occasionally.
  • Fluency in English.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

title: Senior Staff Engineer Software
jobDescription:

Your Role

  • Develop, sustain and evangelize dev Ops methodology withing the organization for software and firmware development
  • Take complete ownership of product delivery infrastructure development and operations

  • Automate Infrastructure provisioning and development processes

  • Experience with Log Aggregation tools like ELK, etc.
  • Understanding of at least one scripting language Python/bash/Perl
  • Proficiency with modern development tools, like Git, Bitbucket, Jira, Confluence etc.
  • Open Shift pipelines
  • Exposure to microservices tools landscape, e.g., Prometheus/Grafana, Tracing, service mesh etc.

title: Web Content Strategist (m/f/d)
jobDescription:
We are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website.
  • Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies).
  • Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions.
  • Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally.
  • Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization.
  • Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation.
  • Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution.



Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks.
  • Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines.
  • A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities.
  • Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic.
  • Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities.
  • Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance.
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders.
  • Industry Knowledge: Semiconductor industry experience is a significant advantage.


#We Are In for driving decarbonization and digitalization.
As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and Io T, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure Io T. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} We are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website.
  • Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies).
  • Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions.
  • Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally.
  • Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization.
  • Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation.
  • Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution.



Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks.
  • Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines.
  • A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities.
  • Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic.
  • Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities.
  • Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance.
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders.
  • Industry Knowledge: Semiconductor industry experience is a significant advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website. Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies). Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions. Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally. Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization. Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation. Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks. Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines. A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities. Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic. Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities. Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance. Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.

If you believe you belong to any of the categories of protected Veterans listed above, please indicate by checking the appropriate box below. description:
We are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website.
  • Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies).
  • Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions.
  • Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally.
  • Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization.
  • Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation.
  • Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution.



Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks.
  • Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines.
  • A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities.
  • Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic.
  • Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities.
  • Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance.
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders.
  • Industry Knowledge: Semiconductor industry experience is a significant advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. Data": {"display Banner": false, "display Text": ""}} We are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally

Your Role

Key responsibilities in your new role

  • Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website.
  • Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies).
  • Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions.
  • Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally.
  • Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization.
  • Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation.
  • Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution.



Your Profile

Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

  • Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks.
  • Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines.
  • A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities.
  • Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic.
  • Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities.
  • Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance.
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders.
  • Industry Knowledge: Semiconductor industry experience is a significant advantage.

This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A \"disabled veteran\" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A \"recently separated veteran\" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An \"active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran\" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An \"Armed forces service medal veteran\" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. are Looking for a professional to drive website governance by standardizing content structures, eliminating duplication, and ensuring consistent placement across platforms. The role involves training stakeholders, aligning with PIM processes, implementing governance frameworks, and tracking compliance to improve content quality and efficiency globally Your Role Key responsibilities in your new role Create and maintain detailed website governance rules, including all types of content (e.g., images, documents, trainings, videos, parameters, etc.) and their placement on the website. Eliminate redundant practices, like inconsistent content placement or duplications (e.g., the same document uploaded multiple times with different hierarchies). Standardize structural and technical details for similar product categories to achieve clarity and alignment across divisions. Train divisions and stakeholders on the rules, guidelines, and governance framework, making sure they are understood and adopted globally. Set up a governance framework with clear processes to communicate new rules and guidelines and ensure they are implemented effectively across the organization. Work with the PIM Team to align content management processes with central governance and web publishing standards, creating a seamless end-to-end flow for content implementation. Develop a process to track compliance with governance guidelines and provide feedback loops to improve adoption and execution. Your Profile Qualifications and skills to help you succeed Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience as Web Content Manager or similar role, ideally at a large, decentralized organization transitioning toward centralized governance and frameworks. Expertise in creating and implementing web content governance frameworks, rules, and guidelines. A track record of developing scalable processes and establishing buy-in across diverse teams with differing priorities. Strong understanding of web user journeys, conversion best practices, and content placement to support business growth objectives such as lead generation and organic traffic. Experience working with PIM systems, web publishing workflows, and collaborating with technical teams (e.g., UX, IT, and Web Teams) to implement functionalities. Familiarity with SEO-driven web content management and understanding of the relationship between content structure, hierarchy, and traffic performance. Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to foster support and accountability across divisional teams and stakeholders. This employer is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as amended by the Jobs for Veterans Act of 2002, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), which requires Government contractors to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment:
1. Disabled veterans
2. Recently separated veterans
3. Active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans
4. Armed Forces service medal veterans

These classifications are defined as follows:
• A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: A veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.
• A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.
• An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.
• An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Protected veterans may have additional rights under USERRA - the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act. In particular, if you were absent from employment in order to perform service in the uniformed service, you may be entitled to be reemployed by your employer in the position you would have obtained with reasonable certainty if not for the absence due to service. For more information, call the U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS), toll- free, at 1-866-4-USA-DOL.
